svg.text: How the app runs on one DigitalOcean droplet, how a change gets there, and where the backups go. Values in <angle brackets> are placeholders: no hostnames, IPs or secrets in the repository.
Caddy asks for and renews it
Ubuntu x86-64 · 1 vCPU · 512 MB RAM + 2 GB swap · key-only SSH, fail2ban · Docker Engine
docker-compose.deploy.yml + .env · pulls the images, never builds
nginx serving the React + Vite build
all data in the pgdata volume
backup.sh auto: one dump a day
Actions does the building and starts every deploy
CI on every PR and on main: make lint, make test
a merge alone changes nothing on the server
also runs inside a deploy when “build” is ticked
checks both images exist on Docker Hub
the server keeps the current and the previous tag
1. Merge the pull request into main. Nothing changes on the server yet.
2. Actions › Expense tracker deploy › Run workflow on main, with “build” ticked: the images workflow pushes sha-<commit>.
3. The runner checks both images exist, then connects over SSH and sends only: deploy sha-<commit>.
4. deploy-gate.sh refreshes the compose file, backup.sh and deploy.sh from main, then runs deploy.sh.
5. deploy.sh: backup → pull → IMAGE_TAG in .env → compose up --wait → check nginx and the API → remove older images.
Roll back: run the deploy again with the previous tag. If that version ran a migration, restore the backup it took.
Public: only Caddy on 80/443. SSH is key-only.
frontend binds 127.0.0.1; backend and db aren't published.
The deploy key can redeploy an existing image, nothing else.
The login page is public: 5 wrong tries lock an email 15 min.
.env and rclone.conf exist only on the server.
